_comment: VENDOR PRICING TABLE, TRANSCRIBED VERBATIM. This file is data, not logic —
when rates change, edit the numbers here and bump rates_version. Nothing
else needs to change. lib/pricing.mjs reads this and does arithmetic only.
Source: https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/pricing
Fetched: 2026-08-04. All figures USD per million tokens (MTok).
The four cache columns are stored EXPLICITLY rather than derived from
input x multiplier, even though today every row satisfies 1.25x / 2x / 0.1x
exactly. Storing them verbatim means a future vendor change that breaks that
relationship gets priced correctly instead of silently wrong. A test asserts
the invariant still holds, so a transcription typo fails loudly (see
test/pricing-config.test.mjs).
MODEL IDS: every model carries an `ids` block naming it on all three
platforms, because we reach Claude through the Keystone Bedrock gateway and
a Bedrock id is NOT the Claude API id. Only `ids.anthropic` is used for
matching (`prefix` is derived from it); `ids.bedrock` and `ids.vertex` are
carried so lib/pricing.mjs's normalizeModelId can be TESTED against the real
strings each platform emits. A form we fail to normalize prices to null, and
null is what these ids are here to prevent. Source for the id spellings:
https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/models/model-ids-and-versions

cache_multipliers._comment: Vendor-stated multipliers vs base input price. Retained for the invariant check and for pricing a model whose explicit cache columns are absent.

_comment: How each platform spells the SAME model. lib/pricing.mjs matches on the
Claude API form only; normalizeModelId() rewrites the others into it.
Documented here so a reader can see WHY the normalizer does what it does,
and so the per-model `ids` blocks below have a legend.

anthropic.label: Claude API (first-party) — the canonical form we match on
anthropic.aliases: Pre-4.6 models also accept a dateless alias (claude-sonnet-4-5) that points at the newest dated snapshot. Both forms prefix-match the same entry, so both price correctly.
anthropic.note: Claude Platform on AWS uses these ids too, NOT Bedrock-style ones.

bedrock.label: Amazon Bedrock — what the Keystone gateway is most likely to emit
bedrock.v1_suffix: Claude Opus 4.6 (anthropic.claude-opus-4-6-v1) is the LAST id to carry -v1. Dropped from Sonnet 4.6 onward.
bedrock.region_prefixes: Regional and cross-region inference profiles prepend a region scope: us. / eu. / apac. / global. — giving TWO dotted prefixes (us.anthropic.claude-opus-5). The normalizer must strip repeatedly; stripping once leaves 'anthropic.' and prices to null. This was a real bug, fixed 2026-08-04.
bedrock.pricing_note: Regional and multi-region endpoints carry a 10% premium over global, for Sonnet 4.5 / Haiku 4.5 / Opus 4.5 and later. Not applied — see not_implemented.data_residency_1_1x. Bedrock is invoiced by AWS, so its rate card is independent of the ones in this file.

vertex.label: Google Cloud Vertex AI
vertex.format_before_4_6: claude-{name}-{major}-{minor}@{YYYYMMDD} — an @ where the Claude API uses a dash
vertex.note: The normalizer rewrites @YYYYMMDD to -YYYYMMDD rather than stripping it: the date distinguishes real snapshots and dropping it would match a shorter prefix.

not_a_model_id._comment: Values seen in the `model` position on this machine that must price to NULL, never to a guess. Friendly aliases are echoes of slash-command input; <synthetic> is a harness placeholder with every token field 0; the non-Claude ids are other Bedrock-hosted vendors reachable through the same gateway.

_comment: Extra prefixes that must resolve to a model above. Kept as data so a naming
convention we did not anticipate is a config edit, not a code change.
Matched by the same longest-prefix rule as `models`, AFTER normalization.
The 3.x family inverts word order (claude-3-5-haiku vs claude-haiku-4-5),
so Haiku 3.5's real id does not prefix-match its own `prefix` field. The
alias is what actually makes it price. Its `prefix` is retained because
records already stamp model_prefix and changing it would break re-pricing.

not_implemented._comment: Vendor pricing modifiers this instrument does NOT apply, each with why. Recorded so a future reader knows they were considered rather than missed.
not_implemented.batch_api_50pct_discount: Batch halves input and output. Claude Code makes interactive Messages API calls, never batch, so the discount can never apply here.
not_implemented.data_residency_1_1x: Claude 4.6+ with inference_geo:'us' bills 1.1x on ALL token categories. Bedrock regional (vs global) endpoints carry a similar 10% premium. NOT DETECTABLE: inference_geo is a request field and does not appear in the transcript usage object, so we cannot tell which endpoint served a call. If our Keystone Bedrock gateway pins a region, EVERY figure this instrument produces is 10% low — uniformly, so comparisons between runs stay valid while absolute dollars do not. Unresolved; see COST.md.
not_implemented.web_search_10_per_1000: Server-side web search bills $10/1,000 searches on top of tokens. Measured: server_tool_use is {web_search_requests:0, web_fetch_requests:0} on all 162,839 occurrences across every transcript on this machine, so the term is exactly zero here. Web fetch is free by vendor terms regardless. If a future skill enables server-side search, this becomes real and the raw usage object already carries the counter needed to price it.
not_implemented.code_execution_0_05_per_hour: $0.05/container-hour past 1,550 free hours/month, and free when used alongside web search or fetch. Billed on wall-clock, not tokens, and not reported per call in the transcript. Out of scope for a token instrument.
not_implemented.managed_agents_session_runtime: $0.08 per session-hour for Claude Managed Agents. Claude Code is not Managed Agents.
not_implemented.long_context_premium: None to implement — vendor states Claude 4.6+ include the full 1M context at standard rates, so there is no >200K tier to model.

cross_model_caveat._comment: Not a price, but it distorts any comparison made in TOKENS instead of dollars.
cross_model_caveat.tokenizer_change: Claude 4.7+ and Mythos Preview use a newer tokenizer producing approximately 30% MORE tokens for the same text (exact figure varies by content). Sonnet 4.6 and earlier use the previous one. So a token-volume comparison across that boundary is inflated ~30% for the newer model even at identical work, and 'cheaper in tokens' can mean 'more expensive in dollars'. Compare dollars across that line, or tokens only within one tokenizer generation.
